notes: Asthma with no recent breathlessness or wheeze, no emergency visit and SpO2 94% or above. Favour walking, chair and standing strength, and breathing exercises; always warm up; stop and rest if wheezy or tight in the chest; avoid smoke, dust and cold air.
patient_advice: Always warm up first. Carry your inhaler. If you cough, wheeze or feel tight in the chest, stop and rest, and see your doctor if it doesn't settle. Keep away from smoke, dust and traffic; exercise indoors on smoky, very cold or very hot days. Don't exercise during a bad spell of asthma.

notes: Fungal skin infection (tinea, ringworm). Sweat and damp skin slow healing.
patient_advice: Exercise when it is cool, in loose cotton clothes. Afterwards wash with lukewarm water, dry well (skin folds, between the toes; the infected area last) and change into dry clothes and socks; don't share towels. Keep the infected area dry; no cream on it unless the doctor prescribed one. If the skin is broken or oozing, do lighter exercise and tell your doctor.

notes: Dermatitis, eczema or psoriasis: not catching. Sweat and heat bring on the itch.
patient_advice: Exercise when it is cool, in loose cotton clothes; drink water. Afterwards rinse with lukewarm water and a mild soap, pat dry and put on your moisturiser straight away. During a flare, do lighter exercise. If the skin is broken or oozing, do lighter exercise and tell your doctor. It is not catching.
